problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [-1,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5y.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1.2,\,-0.3]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8xy+2x \\ 4{x}^{2}+2y-5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(8xy+2x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}+2y-5) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(8xy+2x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}+2y-5)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x \\ 8x & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x \\ 8x & 2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}8xy+2x \\ 4{x}^{2}+2y-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x \\ 8x & 2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}8xy+2x \\ 4{x}^{2}+2y-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.2 \\ -0.3\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}8(-0.3)+2 & 8(1.2) \\ 8(1.2) & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}8(1.2)(-0.3)+2(1.2) \\ 4(1.2)^{2}+2(-0.3)-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.2 \\ -0.3\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-0.4 & 9.6 \\ 9.6 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-0.48 \\ 0.16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.2 \\ -0.3\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-0.4)\cdot 2-(9.6)\cdot (9.6)}[\begin{aligned}2 & -9.6 \\ -9.6 & -0.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-0.48 \\ 0.16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.2 \\ -0.3\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{92.96}[\begin{aligned}-2.496 \\ 4.544\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.173 \\ -0.251\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
